meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.
Did you hear about this face, though?
I was busy today because of face, though.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.
Please don't say it like that.
It's not that difficult compared to what I thought.

meanings.en: to be fun, to be entertaining
meanings.note: Spoken contraction of 재미있다.

examples.trans: This movie is really fun.
Studying Korean is fun.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 이렇게 아무 말도 않고 계속 가기만 하면 너무 재미가 없는데.
examples.trans: If we just keep walking without saying a word, the footage will be too boring.
The topic of fun, interest came up during this shoot.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: What time is it now?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 근데 저 웃음소리는 어디서 나는 거냐, 안 웃길 때도 막 나는 거냐?
examples.trans: Where is that laughter coming from—does it play even when nothing is funny?
Here the word for 'sound of laughter' is key.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

meanings.note: used in 막을 내리다 / 막 내리다 ('to bring down the curtain', i.e., to end a show or era)

examples.trans: The performance came to an end.

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (pron).

examples.text: 저거 봤어? 앞에서 웃다가 가자마자 표정 싹 바뀌는 거 봤어?
examples.trans: Did you see that? Smiling in front of him and changing her expression completely the second he walked away?
Here the word for 'that' is key.
